why_next: The overlap-controlled FP-TP experiment partially resolves the parent's threshold tautology: FP becomes nonzero at 75% overlap (0.0958) and threshold shifts to 0.25 at 100% overlap (FP=0.35). However, the overlap design is materially flawed — the uniform-shift implementation (shift=overlap_pct/100*0.09) produces 0% actual distributional overlap at the 25% and 50% conditions, so FP=0 at those conditions is a design artifact, not evidence against discrimination. The coarse threshold grid [0.20,0.25,...0.80] cannot locate the true optimum between 0.20 and 0.25. A corrected overlap design (Gaussian distributions with controlled area overlap, or symmetric failure-distribution shift) is required to test whether the threshold increases gradually under genuine moderate overlap. This is a higher-information follow-up than attempting another mock-to-production attempt, because without validating discrimination under genuine moderate overlap on mock, the production substrate cannot meaningfully test it either. The parent's production-substrate question remains open but this mock-level gap must be closed first.
